recentItems.title: Russia Adds Su-34 Fighter-Bombers In War Fleet To Shred Ukraine As Zelenskyy Goes Begging In Europe
recentItems.description:
Russia has delivered another batch of Su-34 fighter-bombers, maintaining the production of this essential strike aircraft, which has played a significant role in conducting standoff attacks throughout the conflict in Ukraine.

The Russian government reports that these aircraft are undergoing continuous enhancements informed by insights gained from combat operations.

Since the onset of the war in Ukraine, there has been a significant surge in the delivery rate of Su-34 aircraft.

This uptick underscores the critical role that this platform plays in Russian military strategy, as well as Moscow's determination to both replenish and enhance its tactical aviation capabilities.

The Su-34 fighter-bomber is a two-seat multi-functional aircraft.

The Su-34 is designed for all-weather and round-the-clock engagement of ground and surface targets.

The Su-34 is capable of smashing fortified targets at considerable distances from home airfields.

The aircraft can destroy air targets in an intense enemy counter-fire and electronic countermeasure environment.

The Su-34 is capable of performing individual and group electronic countermeasure cover.

The formidable warplane is also capable of performing aerial reconnaissance.

Russian Su-34 aircraft are spelling doom with glide bombs.

A glide bomb is a stand-off weapon with flight controls which allow it to use a gliding flight path onto a target at a greater distance.

These weapons allow Russia to supplement an inadequate inventory of tactical air-launched missiles.

They also help Russia avoid using free-fall bombs that expose pilots to a greater risk of being shot down.

Russia is using glide bombs, along with direct-attack munitions, in volume to overwhelm Ukrainian air defenses.

Russia has the capacity to produce more glide bomb kits for older Fab series bombs than Kyiv has to resupply its defense systems’ ammunition.

Therefore, shooting them down directly is not a sustainable strategy...

recentItems.title: Russia Builds Drone Attack Base In Just 6 Weeks, Putin's Jet-Powered UAVs Test Zelenskyy's Ukraine
recentItems.description:
In a remarkable feat, Russia is nearing the completion of a significant new facility designed for the launch of jet-powered drones, with its construction rapidly progressing in a mere six weeks.

Reuters News Agency analyzed commercial imagery provided by Planet Labs and Airbus.

The site in what was an empty field in ‌Russia's southwestern Rostov region on August 31 had become a complex facility the size of around 126 soccer pitches this week.

The ongoing construction aligns with a noticeable increase in the deployment of Russian jet-powered attack drones targeting Ukraine.

Ukraine is finding it difficult to intercept these rapid weapons capable of reaching speeds as high as 600 kilometers per hour.

recentItems.title: US Hindu Temple Mass Shooting Bid: Chicago Scare Averted In Nick Of Time, Teen Told Coworker This
recentItems.description:
Authorities in a Chicago suburb revealed that they successfully prevented a possible mass shooting, apprehending a 19-year-old individual believed to have intended to attack a Hindu temple.

Alexandros Paporakis, a Taco Bell cashier from Palatine, Illinois, is confronting serious felony charges for making a terrorist threat and for the unlawful possession of weapons.

Authorities suspect that he intended to attack the largest Hindu temple located in Aurora, Illinois; however, the precise site he aimed for is still being examined.

At this time, it is uncertain whether Paporakis has secured legal counsel.
